name: THE JOBS OFFICE
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461 (more boards), 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428, 441.
facts: WORLD's real place (records/target/bb/real_places.json, 'the_unemployment_office'): Nevada JobConnect, 3405 South Maryland Parkway east of the Strip; in 2020 Nevada had the worst unemployment in the country and the lines for these offices ran round the block; 'in the collapse the line never went home: it is where a company finds men who need work'.

A state job office's public floor is a claims hall: numbered windows behind glass along one wall, banks of joined chairs facing them, queue barriers, a ticket kiosk at the door; beside it the resource room: rows of computer terminals for the job search, printers, the job boards, and a workshop room of folding tables.
On house tiles a bank of joined chairs is slow going and low cover; a job board on its stand is solid and hides a man; a window's glass is seen through and never crossed.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (jobsoffice_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The jobs office is its own map kind, one cell: eight fights in ten there are fought inside it, by the cell's own dice; the rest in the line outside.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words); 'sight' says whether a blocker hides a man ('blocked', the obstacles row) or is seen past ('seen'). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The office's block wall: no way through, no sight through.

floor.effect: The office's worn carpet tiles: open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

glass.effect: A claims window's glass on its counter, its number still lit in a dead sign: nobody passes; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its palisade you see through.

counter.effect: The counter between two windows, waist high: low cover. [bb] its palisade, waist high.

desks.effect: The caseworkers' desks behind the windows, pushed over: cover.

files.effect: Steel file cabinets of claims, tipped over: cover.

barriers.effect: Queue barriers, posts and belts knotted together into a low fence: low cover.

chairs.effect: A bank of joined waiting chairs, bolted to the floor: low cover, and slow going over them (3 AP). [bb] its brush.
chairs.say: Waiting chairs: slow going, low cover.

bins.effect: Bins, overflowing with forms: low cover.

vending.effect: A vending machine on its face: cover.

planters.effect: Concrete planters, the plants long dead: cover.

kiosk.effect: The ticket kiosk, its screen smashed, its last number still on the roll: cover.

bedrolls.effect: Bedrolls and packs where the line slept and kept its place: low cover.

boards.effect: The job boards on their stands, papered over and over: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through them. [bb] its wall.

terminals.effect: A row of job-search terminals on their desks, the screens dark: cover.

tables.effect: The workshop room's folding tables, on their sides: cover.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a waste bin. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The office's doors, open, the line outside them: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in jobsoffice_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: a one-storey office of carpet and glass.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the office's drop ceiling, its tiles fallen in places, its 'now serving' signs dead, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the casino's coffers).
